source: Carlo Gavazzi Controls, WM3-96 Serial Communication Protocol, Vers. 1 Rev. 3 (July 7th, 2005)
notes: Modbus RTU on RS-485 (1200 to 9600 baud, parity none, even or odd, 1 stop bit, set on the meter) or RS-232 (fixed 9600 baud, no parity, 1 stop bit). Slave address 1 to 255; the manual gives a default address of 1 and parity none, but no usable baud default. Answer time-out 300 ms.

The meter supports only function 04 (read, at most 120 words), function 06 (write one word) and function 08 (check frame). There is no function 03: values are in the input area, and the writable items (configuration, remote outputs and counter reset commands) are listed as holding registers although this device reads them with function 04 as well.

Addresses are the hexadecimal values of the ADDRESS column of the manual, used as the Modbus data address as printed (for example W L1 is read with data address 0008, two words), address base 0. The manual steps each 4-byte variable by 4 in these addresses.

Instantaneous variables (0x000 to 0x0E7) are 4-byte integers, most significant byte first. Voltage, current and power are raw integers whose scale comes from the three range codes at 0x0E8 and 0x0EA (value = raw x 10^(code - 6) in V, A or W/VA/var; the power code is increased when the value exceeds 9999). Because the scale is a code and not an exponent, scale_factor cannot express it and no unit is attached to those registers.

Above address 0x0E8 the meter sends 16-bit and 32-bit values least significant byte first, so those registers have byte order little (and word order little for 32-bit values). Energy counters are 5-byte: the low 4 bytes are a signed integer (resolution 10 Wh, so kWh = value / 100) and the high byte, held in a separate area, is multiplied by 10^9 before the division; the high byte is signed in the manual but is mapped here as unsigned.

Not mapped: the monthly energy counters, the event log, the real-time clock area, the EEPROM data-format tables (digital and analogue output, pulse type, FFT enable, language and similar settings) and the 5th-byte layout of the monthly counters. Harmonic values are valid only when the FFT is enabled for the phase.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
